Cluster Resampling

Source: R/bootstrap_objects.R
cluster_resample.Rd

Selects the cluster bootstrap: every replicate draws the groups of observations with replacement and refits the model on them.

Usage

cluster_resample(cluster, data = NULL)

Arguments

cluster

A one-sided formula with one variable, as in ~ id.

data

A data frame with that variable and one row for each observation of the fit, or NULL. With NULL the data frame is the data of the call that built the fit.

Value

A ClusterResample object, inheriting from resample_method, with the properties cluster and data.

Details

The groups are the values of the variable that the formula names, a column of data. A fit does not keep its data: with data = NULL the data frame is the data argument of the call of statmod(), evaluated in the environment of the model formula, and an error says to pass data where that fails or where its number of rows is not the fit's. The variable must have no missing values. A group drawn \(k\) times gives all its observations the count \(k\). Without random effects the likelihood is a sum over observations, so this is the fit to the duplicated groups with the design held.

Beside a modelterms7::random() term the groups drawn more than once become new groups: each copy of a cluster has its own groups, with an effect of its own, as in Stata's bootstrap, cluster() idcluster(). A weight is not enough in this case, because the prior of the effects would count a group drawn twice once. The grouping variable of each random-effect term is relabeled in the replicate when every one of its groups lies in a single cluster (the groups of a term that is the cluster variable itself, or nested in it). A grouping variable that spans several clusters keeps its labels, and its effects are shared by the copies. The design is rebuilt on the rows drawn: the other terms are reapplied with modelterms7::term_predict(), so a basis keeps the knots of the fit and a factor its contrasts, and the random-effect terms are built on the new groups with the hyperparameters of the fit.

The individual effects of different replicates are effects of different groups, so no remapping between replicates exists. The replicates store the coordinates that every replicate has: the coefficients of the other terms, and with refit = "full" the hyperparameters, the variance components among them. The coordinates of the individual random effects are missing in the stored matrix, and their rows and columns in the variance are NA. A term that shares a covariance through a label, a smooth random effect (modelterms7::RandomSmoothTerm()) and a random effect inside the subformula of another term are rejected.

See also

resample_method for the comparison of the three schemes, add_bootstrap() and bootstrap_vcov() for the functions that take it.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(g = rep(1:12, each = 5), x = runif(60))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(12)[dd$g] + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
fit <- add_bootstrap(fit, n = 30, resample = cluster_resample(~ g))
statmod_bootstrap(fit)
#>       resample        refit replicates replaced error mode_error unidentified
#> 1 cluster (~g) coefficients         30        0     0          0            0

# beside a random intercept the groups drawn again are new groups
fit_re <- statmod(y ~ x + random(~ 1 | g),
                  distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
fit_re <- add_bootstrap(fit_re, n = 10, resample = cluster_resample(~ g))
round(sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_re, vcov_type = bootstrap_vcov(
  resample = cluster_resample(~ g)))))[1:2], 3)
#> mu:(Intercept)           mu:x 
#>          0.347          0.223
